::: {#exr-miller-int-power-substitution}
#### Substitution with a polynomial power

Adapted from @problifesavercalc, Question 1.1.37.

Evaluate the integral:

$$\int_0^3 (x^3 + 3x)^8 (x^2 + 1)\,dx$$
:::

::: {#sol-miller-int-power-substitution}
Let $u = x^3 + 3x$. Then:

$$
\begin{aligned}
du
&= (3x^2 + 3)\,dx \\
&= 3(x^2 + 1)\,dx \\
\implies (x^2 + 1)\,dx
&= \frac{du}{3}
\end{aligned}
$$

Limits:

- When $x = 0$: $u = 0$.
- When $x = 3$:

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  u &= 3^3 + 3(3) \\
  &= 27 + 9 \\
  &= 36.
  \end{aligned}
  $$

Substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\int_0^3 (x^3 + 3x)^8 (x^2 + 1)\,dx
&= \frac{1}{3}\int_0^{36} u^8\,du \\
&= \frac{1}{3}\sb{\frac{u^9}{9}}_0^{36} \\
&= \frac{36^9}{27}
\end{aligned}
$$
:::
